'''Harold Golombek'''<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://timarit.is/page/3212738#page/n5/mode/2up |title=Vandræðabarnið Mecking |last=Svavarsson |first=Svavar Guðni |website=Timarit.is |access-date=15 October 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/viewer/bl/0000619/19520101/010/0010 |title=Birmingham Daily Post, 1 January 1952 |via=[[British Newspaper Archive]] |access-date=15 October 2024}}</ref>
<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/938808963/ |title=Evening Chronicle from Manchester, 26 April 1950 |website=Newspapers.com |date=26 April 1950 |access-date=15 October 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://dilemaveche.ro/sectiune/dileme-on-line/din-istoria-revistei-romane-de-sah-1947-1950-621917.html |title=Din istoria Revistei Române de șah, 1947-1950 (III) |last=Amandi |first=Ionuţ  |website=Dilemaveche.ro |access-date=15 October 2024}}</ref> [[Order of the British Empire|OBE]] (1 March 1911 – 7 January 1995) was a British [[chess]] player, chess author, and wartime codebreaker.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hartston |first=William |date=1995-01-10 |title=Obituary: Harry Golombek |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/obituary-harry-golombek-1567343.html |access-date=2023-03-15}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Upton |first=John |date=2021-01-07 |title=Remembering GM Harry Golombek OBE (01-III-1911 07-I-1995) |work=British Chess News |url=http://britishchessnews.com/2021/01/07/remembering-harry-golombek-obe-01-03-1911-07-i-1995/ |access-date=2023-03-15}}</ref> He was three times [[British Chess Championship|British chess champion]], in 1947, 1949, and 1955 and finished second in 1948.
==Biography==
He was born in [[Lambeth]] to [[Polish-Jewish]]<ref>{{cite journal |last=Sugarman |first=Martin |year=2005 |title=Breaking the codes: Jewish personnel at Bletchley Park |journal=Jewish Historical Studies |volume=40 |pages=217 |jstor=24027033}}</ref> parents. He was the chess correspondent of the newspaper ''[[The Times]]'' from 1945 to 1985, after [[Stuart Milner-Barry]]. He was a [[FIDE]] official, and served as arbiter for several important events, including the [[Candidates' Tournament]] of 1959 in [[Yugoslavia]], and the 1963 World Chess Championship match between [[Mikhail Botvinnik]] and [[Tigran Petrosian]]. He also edited the game collections of [[José Raúl Capablanca|Capablanca]] and [[Richard Réti|Réti]], and was a respected author. He was editor of ''[[British Chess Magazine]]'' from 1938 to 1940, and its overseas editor in the 1960s and 1970s. Golombek also translated several chess books from Russian into English.

On the outbreak of [[World War II]] in September 1939, Golombek was in [[Buenos Aires]], [[Argentina]], competing in the [[Chess Olympiad]] for Britain alongside [[C. H. O'D. Alexander]] and [[Stuart Milner-Barry]].<ref>[[Stuart Milner-Barry]], "Hut 6: Early Days", p. 89 in F. H. Hinsley and Alan Stripp, eds. Codebreakers: The Inside Story of Bletchley Park, Oxford University Press, 1993</ref> They immediately returned to the UK, and were soon recruited into [[Bletchley Park]], the wartime [[codebreaking]] centre. Golombek worked in [[Hut 8]],<ref>[[David Kahn (writer)|David Kahn]], ''Seizing the Enigma'', 1991, {{ISBN|0-395-42739-8}}, p. 139</ref> the section responsible for solving German Naval [[Enigma machine|Enigma]], moving to another section in October/November 1942.<ref>Ralph Erskine, "Breaking German Naval Enigma", p. 186 in ''Action this Day'', edited by Ralph Erskine and Michael Smith, 2001</ref> After the war he lived at 35 Albion Crescent, [[Chalfont St Giles]]. He was unusual among public figures in replying with care to letters from unknown people, such as young schoolboys, from this address.

Golombek represented England nine times in the Chess Olympiad.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.olimpbase.org/players/6y6omc8f.html |title=Men's Chess Olympiads: Harry Golombek |last=Bartelski |first=Wojciech |website=OlimpBase |access-date=19 November 2019}}</ref> He earned the title of [[International Master]] in 1950 and was awarded that of [[Grandmaster (chess)#Honorary grandmasters|Honorary Grandmaster]] in 1985.<ref>Golombek himself always disputed that his Grandmaster title was 'honorary', insisting that it was belatedly bestowed for his playing achievements in the 1940s (see {{cite news |last=Hartston |first=William |author-link=William Hartston |date=10 January 1995 |title=Obituary: Harry Golombek |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/obituary-harry-golombek-1567343.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220509/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/obituary-harry-golombek-1567343.html |archive-date=9 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |newspaper=[[The Independent]] |access-date=1 May 2019}}).</ref><ref name=shorthistory>Allport, D.H. & Friskney, N.J. "A Short History of Wilson's School", Wilson's School Charitable Trust, 1987</ref> He was the first British player to qualify for an [[Interzonal]] tournament.

Golombek studied [[philology]] at [[King's College London]],<ref name="bhsm">[http://www.dcs.warwick.ac.uk/bshm/zingaz/LondonPeopleD.html#gol British Society for the History of Mathematics Gazetteer]</ref> having been a pupil at [[Wilson's School|Wilson's Grammar School]], Camberwell.<ref name=shorthistory/> He was appointed OBE in 1966, the first to be so honoured for services to chess.<ref name="bhsm"/>

Golombek died 7 January 1995.<ref>{{cite news |date=January 19, 1995 |title=Harry Golombek, Chess Writer, 83 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1995/01/19/obituaries/harry-golombek-chess-writer-83.html |url-access=subscription |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> 
==Books==
[[File:Hoogovens schaaktoernooi, Bestanddeelnr 903-1810.jpg|thumb|Hoogovens 1949: Golombek vs. [[Alberic O'Kelly de Galway]] ]]
* ''The World Chess Championship 1948'', 1948, David McKay 
* ''World Chess Championship 1954'', 1954, MacGibbon and Kee
* ''[[iarchive:retisbestgamesof0000reti/mode/2up|Reti's Best Games of Chess]]'', 1954, G. Bell & Sons, republished 1974, Dover
* [[iarchive:gameofchess00golo|''The Game of Chess'']], 3rd edition,1980, Penguin
* ''The World Chess Championship 1957'', 1957, MacGibbon and Kee
* ''Instructions to Young Chess Players'', 1958, Pitman {{ISBN|0-273-48550-4}}
* ''Modern Opening Chess Strategy'', 1959, Pitman 
* ''4th Candidates Tournament 1959: Bled, Zagreb, Belgrade'' (originally BCM Quarterly No.3), 1960, BCM
* ''Capablanca's Hundred Best Games of Chess'', 1947, G. Bell and Sons
* ''[[iarchive:fischervspasskyw0000golo/page/n5/mode/2up|Fischer v Spassky: The World Chess Championship 1972]]'', 1973, Barrie & Jenkins
* ''[[iarchive:ChessAHistoryByHarryGolombek/mode/2up|Chess: A History]],'' 1976, Putnam
* ''Improve Your Chess'', 1976, Pitman 
* ''The Best Games of C.H.O'D. Alexander'' (co-authored with William Hartston), 1976, Oxford University Press
* ''[[iarchive:golombeksencyclo0000golo/page/n5/mode/2up|Golombek's Encyclopedia of Chess]]'' (Golombek as editor-in-chief), 1977, Crown
* ''Beginning Chess'', 1981, Penguin {{ISBN|978-0140464122}}
